passage: Teacher's note, Class 5. Akash came to my desk before the trip and asked, “Ma'am, may I go to the shop across the road? I need a pencil, and I'll be back before the bell.” I told him no, because the road is busy and I could not see him from the gate. He nodded, but I could tell he was disappointed. I said, “If you ask me at break, I will send him with the peon.” Akash said, “Okay.” He came back at break, and I sent him with the peon. I think clear reasons help a child accept no. Ms. Aparna.

qa.q: Who was sent with Akash to the shop?
What was Akash probably feeling when he nodded after hearing no?
qa.a: He was probably disappointed but understood, since Ms. Aparna gave a clear reason about the busy road.

qa.q: What did Ms. Aparna do that made a no easier to accept?
qa.a: She gave a reason about safety and offered another way, sending him at break with the peon.

qa.q: How might Akash's request look from Ms. Aparna's side?
qa.a: She could not see him from the gate and worried about the busy road, so her no was about his safety and not about doubting him.

grounding: A child asks may I go and learns that permission depends on safety, timing and trust, and a clear reason helps accept a no.

passage: I watched from the school corridor as Gopika went up to the games teacher. “Sir, can I please stay inside during break? My knee is sore.” The teacher frowned and said, “Show me.” Gopika lifted her trouser hem to show a red patch. The teacher said, “Go to the nurse first and then rest in the library.” Gopika nodded. Arnab, her friend, said, “I thought he'd say no.” “Me too,” said Gopika. I think she was surprised but also relieved. I'm not sure whether the knee hurt as much as she said, but she asked politely and gave a reason.

qa.q: Where did the teacher tell Gopika to go first?
What was Gopika probably feeling when the teacher said yes?
qa.a: She was surprised and relieved, since she had expected a no and said “Me too” to Arnab, though the observer is not sure how much the knee hurt.

qa.q: What did Gopika do that helped her request?
qa.a: She asked politely, gave a reason and showed the sore knee when asked.

qa.q: Why might the teacher have asked to see the knee?
qa.a: He may have wanted to check it was real and safe to skip play, which is part of how permission depends on trust.

grounding: A child asks can I please stay inside and permission depends on trust and safety, observed by a bystander.
